# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 4

**1** Fifteen days later — after I had fasted and prayed hard — the meaning of the book's writing was finally opened to me. This is what it said: **2** "Your children have sinned against God, Hermas. They have blasphemed the Lord. They betrayed their own parents out of sheer wickedness — earning themselves the name 'betrayers of parents.' And they didn't even gain anything from their betrayal; they just kept stacking up more sins on top of the ones they already had. **3** Wild living, reckless wickedness — more and more was added, until your children's sins had reached their full measure. **4** But you know that God is full of mercy. If you and your whole household repent together — if you humble yourselves before the Lord and serve him from pure hearts — he will heal every sin of your past." **5** "Don't give up on your family. Keep correcting them, keep calling them back. Think of a goldsmith — he refines his work through fire. That's what God does with his own people, and especially with those who truly belong to him." That was the end of the message.

---

*PNEUMA note: The goldsmith refining by fire (v.5) is a classical image of purifying judgment — cf. Malachi 3:2-3; 1 Peter 1:7. The emphasis on corporate household repentance is notable.*
